tool_input.command:
cat > /tmp/test_scheduled.ts << 'EOF'
import { Post } from './app/Models/Post.js'
import { User } from './app/Models/User.js'

const user = await User.create({
  name: 'Test Author',
  email: `test-${Date.now()}@example.com`,
  password: 'password123',
})

const futureDate = new Date(Date.now() + 7200000).toISOString()
const post = await Post.forceCreate({
  title: 'Test Scheduled Post',
  excerpt: 'This is a test excerpt',
  body: 'This is a test body',
  authorId: user.id,
  publishedAt: futureDate,
})

console.log(`Created post: ${post.id}\t${post.title}\t${post.publishedAt}`)
EOF
bun run /tmp/test_scheduled.ts
tool_input.description: Create a test scheduled post and verify it can be created

result:
Excellent! I have successfully implemented the scheduled post feature. Here's a summary of the changes:

## Implementation Summary

### Database & Schema
- Added `publishedAt` nullable text column to the `posts` table via migration
- Posts with no date or past dates are considered public; future dates make them scheduled

### Model & Validation
- Updated `Post` model to include `publishedAt` in fillable array
- Added `publishAt` optional field to `PostPayloadSchema` with ISO 8601 datetime validation

### Visibility Logic
- Enhanced `PostPolicy` with scheduling awareness:
  - Scheduled posts (future `published_at`) only visible to their author
  - Public posts (null or past `published_at`) visible to everyone
- Updated `PostController`:
  - `index()` filters scheduled posts for non-authors
  - `search()` filters scheduled posts for non-authors  
  - `show()` returns **404** for scheduled posts accessed by non-authors (as required)
  - `store()` and `update()` handle the `publishAt` field

### Frontend
- Added "Publish at" datetime input fields to `posts/New.tsx` and `posts/Edit.tsx`
- Fields are optional; empty/null means "publish immediately"
- Edit page pre-populates existing scheduled date

### API Response
- Updated `PostResourceData` to include `publishedAt` field
- Post objects include the timestamp when returned to the frontend

### Console Command
- Created `posts:scheduled` command that outputs:
  - Format: `<id>\t<title>\t<published_at>` (tab-separated)
  - One line per scheduled post, sorted by publication date (soonest first)
  - Empty output if no posts are scheduled
  - Exit code 0

All 11 tests pass, typecheck is clean, and the implementation follows project conventions.
